activities.title: A mole is a counting word

differentiation.support: Provide the student notes open at the molar mass definition so learners can follow how weighing 12 g of carbon counts one mole before they try n = m / M.

activities.title: A common mistake: one mole of everything weighs the same

differentiation.stretch: Ask learners to explain why one mole of carbon and one mole of water weigh differently before they take the exit ticket.

activities.title: Here is the trap, sprung on purpose

assessmentPoints: Dozen-and-mole answers in the opening activity
Counting answers in the closing worksheet
successCriteria: I can say a mole counts 6.02 × 10²³ particles, just as a dozen counts 12
I can explain why chemists weigh moles instead of counting particles one by one
objectives.text: Explain what a mole means: a counting word for 6.02 × 10²³ particles

assessmentPoints: Carbon balance answers in the second activity
Mass answers in the closing worksheet
successCriteria: I can use n = m / M to turn a mass into moles, such as 12 g of carbon giving 1 mol
I can use mass = moles x molar mass to turn moles into a mass
objectives.text: Use n = m / M and mass = moles x molar mass to convert between mass and moles

assessmentPoints: Ratio answers in the third activity
Trap answers in the fifth activity and the closing exit ticket
successCriteria: I can read the 2 : 1 : 2 mole ratio from 2 H₂ + O₂ → 2 H₂O and scale the whole ratio
I can explain that one mole of different substances has different masses because each has its own molar mass
objectives.text: Use mole ratios from balanced equations, and explain why one mole of different substances has different masses

subject: science
title: The mole: counting atoms by weighing
